text:
Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI)
• In magnet, protons in body (mostly in water) align with
magnetic field
• Radio waves pulsed through the patient
• Protons absorb radiofrequency (RF) current, tilt out of
alignment with magnetic field
• At end of RF pulse, protons emit energy as they “relax”
back to align with the applied magnetic field
• MRI detects the energy released and the time it takes
the protons to realign with the magnetic field
• Tissues “relax” differently, emit characteristic signals
• Computer creates 2D sections, 3D reconstructions
• Clearest images of soft tissues, no ionizing radiation
• Expensive, uncomfortable
• See examples here. See an animated explanation here.
